lines: Welcome to Common Good during the spooky season. Come in, settle yourself, and keep a little room in the evening for something unexpected.
I hope you’re enjoying the company, and that our Halloween pop-up cocktails have been treating you very well.
I can share a recipe to make at home, or a spooky tale left behind by one of my old patrons. I’ve had rather a few.
Welcome to Common Good during the spooky season. A fine evening for good company, curious cocktails, and just a little less certainty than usual.
I hope you’ve been enjoying our Halloween pop-up and its cocktails. We’ve put a good deal of care into making the evening memorable.
There are recipes you can take home, and tales I’ve collected from bar guests over the years. How many years? The ledgers become rather untidy.
Welcome to Common Good during the spooky season. I hope the room, the company, and our Halloween pop-up cocktails have put you in an agreeable mood.
If a cocktail has caught your fancy, I can give you its recipe to keep and make at home when the evening calls for it.
Or I can tell you a spooky tale an old patron shared across the bar. I’ve been listening a while. Long enough to recognize a good opening.
What shall I put before you: a recipe for your home bar, or a spooky tale from one of my old guests?
Would you like to take a little of tonight’s cocktail magic home, or hear what the guests have been telling me after dark?
How much time have you brought with you tonight? I can fit a tale to it. I’ve had plenty of practice making an evening last.
choices: I've got all the time in the world

lines: How long would you like to linger? A few minutes will do nicely, though some of my older guests were in no hurry to finish.
choices: I've got all the time in the world

lines: Before I choose a tale, tell me how long you have to listen. I keep an eye on the clock for the guests’ benefit, mostly.
choices: I've got all the time in the world

lines: How deep shall we let the shadows get? I have a gentle shiver, a proper chill, and a few tales best heard with the lights nearby.
And what sort of company would you like from the dark: something lightly spooky, something that lingers, or something with a rather firmer grip?
Shall we keep the evening gently haunted, make it properly eerie, or open the drawer I usually leave until the room has grown quiet?
Ah, welcome back to Common Good. It’s good to see you again. I had a feeling our little conversation might have another chapter.
Welcome back. The spooky season has been keeping me occupied, but I haven’t forgotten you. I tend to remember good company.
There you are. Welcome back to Common Good. An evening can pick up quite comfortably where another one left off; I’ve seen it happen often enough.
Good to see you again. Welcome back to our corner of the spooky season. Familiar company has a way of making the evening more interesting.
I remember sharing a cocktail recipe with you. If you’ve had a chance to make it, I hope it treated you well.
I shared a recipe with you before. I hope it proves useful whenever you feel like bringing a little of the spooky season home.
I remember the recipe I shared with you. I hope it has given you something pleasant to look forward to on an evening at home.
And I remember sharing a recipe with you, too. I hope it’s useful whenever the mood strikes at home. Good evenings deserve the occasional encore.
There was a cocktail recipe as well. If you’ve had a chance to try it, I hope it added a little character to the evening.
And the recipe I shared is another little piece of the evening to take with you. I hope it comes in handy when the occasion presents itself.
We left a tale unfinished. I’ve kept your place, if you’d like to return to it. The shadows have been remarkably patient.
choices: Pick up where I left off

lines: There’s a story waiting at the point where you left it. Shall we carry on from there, or choose a different corner of the collection?
Very well. A story ought to suit its listener. Let me see what else the guests have left in my keeping.
Of course. We needn’t invite that particular trouble in tonight. I have another tale that may be more to your taste.
Let’s choose again. A different amount of time, a different degree of darkness; there are several ways to spend an evening in this collection.
We can rearrange the evening. Tell me what you’re in the mood for now, and I’ll have another look among the stories.
Nothing in my collection fits that particular combination just now. We can change the time or the level of fright, and give the shelves another chance.
A small gap in my collection. Even a long career leaves a few. Shall we adjust the length, choose a different sort of chill, or return to the bar?
You’ve heard every tale in this part of the collection. We can revisit one, try another length or level of fright, or turn our attention to a recipe.
For that length and degree of darkness, we’ve reached the end of the tales you haven’t heard. An old favorite can bear another telling, if you’d like.
And that is how it was told to me. I’ve kept the words; you may keep whatever follows you home. Shall we find another tale, or look at the recipes?
There we are. Another old guest’s story safely passed along. I can offer you another, or something rather more practical for the home bar.
All the time in the world? A generous offer. I’ve heard it made before. Let’s choose something worth staying for.
Then we needn’t hurry. I’ve never cared for watching a clock while a good story is opening a door.
This one is a little shorter than your window. A small haunting, neatly contained; there will still be time to look over your shoulder afterward.
I have a brief one that comes in under five minutes. Some guests need very few words to leave the room feeling different.
Welcome to Common Good. I hope the spooky season is treating you well. There are cocktail recipes to take home and a few curious stories to keep you company.
Good evening, and welcome to our little corner of the spooky season. Settle in; I have something for the home bar and something for the imagination.
Back at the bar. Shall we open the recipe cabinet, or let another one of the old guests have a word?
What takes your fancy now: a cocktail recipe to keep, or a tale to carry with you a little less conveniently?
Enjoy the rest of your evening at Common Good. I’ll be here if you need anything else. I generally am.
Thank you for the company. Take a good evening home with you, and leave a little room for another visit. I’m seldom in a hurry.
Which of our four Halloween cocktails would you like the recipe for? I can put the details in your keeping for an evening at home.
Let’s find the recipe that caught your interest. Choose a cocktail, and I’ll share what you need to make it at home.
Here is the recipe. You can read it now or keep a copy for the home bar. A useful souvenir of a slightly unusual evening.
There we are. The recipe is ready whenever your own evening calls for it. You can take a copy using the button below.
There we are—the recipe is saved. I hope it comes in handy when you feel like bringing a little of Common Good home.
Safely saved. A small piece of the evening for another occasion. I find the better recipes deserve more than one night.
Your recipe download has started. I’ll keep the recipe here while you collect it; there’s no need to hurry on my account.
The recipe hasn’t made it into your keeping just yet. Let’s try that again; occasionally even the paperwork develops a little character.
That copy didn’t go through. The recipe is still here to read, and we can try making you another copy when you’re ready.
I’ve shown you every tale that fits those choices for now. We can look back over this visit’s suggestions, choose a different sort of story, or turn to the recipes.
That brings us to the end of my suggestions for this particular mood. One may deserve another look, or we can change the selection. The cocktail recipes are available too.
